[News • 19 hours ago Markets look for signs of a rate hike this year, and investors are preparing for the beginning of earnings season](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/rate-hike-readjustment-and-ai-hardware-momentum-what-to-watch-this-week-160059243.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [News • 5 days ago Warsh speaks](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/kevin-warsh-fed-will-not-be-comfortable-with-inflation-above-2-183000837.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [News • 5 days ago Opening bell](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-pull-back-in-wait-for-warsh-to-speak-224748322.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [News • 6 days ago The Supreme Court blocked Trump's bid to fire Fed governor Cook, but gave him sweeping new powers to remove officials elsewhere](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/supreme-court-gives-trump-sweeping-new-powers-to-fire-government-employees-but-says-federal-reserve-is-protected-173040916.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [Breaking News • 7 days ago In a 5-4 vote, the Supreme Court ruled that Fed Governor Lisa Cook can remain in her role for the time being](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/supreme-court-rejects-trumps-firing-of-federal-reserve-governor-for-now-143412808.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). The Federal Reserve [held interest rates steady](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/fed-expected-to-hold-rates-steady-this-week-as-rate-hike-talks-heat-up-and-us-strikes-a-deal-with-iran-100000734.html) in the range of 3.5%-3.75% on Wednesday in a unanimous decision that [comes at a pivotal time](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/kevin-warshs-fed-debut-comes-at-a-pivotal-moment-for-global-monetary-policy-100000451.html) for the Fed and central banks around the world. Stock futures [held steady](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-nasdaq-futures-climb-as-dow-sp-500-stall-ahead-of-fed-rate-decision-225641465.html) as the Federal Open Market Committee headed into the second day of its two-day policy meeting.

[Skip Navigation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html#MainContent). *   [Policy](https://www.cnbc.com/policy/). [SIGN IN](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html#). [Create free account](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html#). [Video 1](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html). ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)A missing dot. Heading into the meeting, Fed watchers had suspected [Warsh wouldn’t submit his outlook](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/16/fed-chair-warsh-expected-to-withhold-dot-from-central-banks-interest-rate-outlook.html), and some anticipated he might look to end the feature altogether. He confirmed at [a news conference](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html) following the decision that he had declined to share a forecast and is forming task forces to overhaul major Fed operations. ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)A shorter statement. In addition to the rate call, which was widely anticipated in financial markets, the [FOMC’s post-meeting statement](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/june-fed-meeting-redline.html) also not only removed prior language seen as a nod toward an easing slant in the future but took a hatchet to the rest of it. ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)Higher inflation forecast. Nonfarm payroll growth again [defied expectations in May](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/05/jobs-report-may-2026.html) with a gain of 172,000 while the unemployment rate, the Fed’s most closely watched metric, was at 4.3%, unchanged over the past year. *   ![Image 14: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Opt-Out Icon](https://static-redesign.cnbcfm.com/dist/17269f1b6083fd5f61be.svg)[Your Privacy Choices](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html).

Aimee Picchi is the associate managing editor for CBS MoneyWatch, where she covers business and personal finance. The Federal Reserve on Wednesday left its benchmark interest rate unchanged amid resurgent inflation, but nearly half of its policymakers said they would support a rate hike later this year. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept the federal funds rate, which affects borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, in its current range of 3.5% to 3.75%**.**Economists had widely expected the central bank to keep rates steady. "You might have already noticed something, a difference in today's policy statement," Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said in a press conference to discuss the Fed's latest interest rate decision. The Fed also released its Summary of Economic Projections(SEP) on Wednesday, which shows that nearly half of FOMC members said they could support a rate hike later this year. Warsh noted that the FOMC's economic projections show the federal funds rate will sit at 3.8% at the end of 2026 and 3.6% at the end of 2027.
